scope: Pinned source comparison and runtime-oracle requirements; zero product execution

findings.official_source: HTTP selects DeleteOperation; JWT path registers DeleteOperation; ACL checks DeleteCapabilityInt. JWT backend PathsSpecial does not list root-protected paths.
findings.candidate_source: The legacy role handler and R2 native owner require update plus sudo.
findings.conclusion: Source-level capability mismatch. A successful delete-only policy and update+sudo-only rejection are expected on the official fixture; actual status/body observations remain due.

findings.official_source: Bare GET selects ReadOperation. Role collection registers ListOperation, while LIST and GET?list=true select ListOperation.
findings.candidate_source: The legacy collection handler and R2 owner treat bare GET as list.
findings.conclusion: Source-level HTTP operation mismatch. Observe both read-only and list-only policies, bare GET, LIST and GET?list=true; do not normalize 403/405/200 outcomes.

findings.operation: POST/PUT JWT named role and config
findings.official_source: The role path registers UpdateOperation; the backend does not mark JWT paths root-protected.
findings.candidate_source: The legacy named-role handler requires update plus sudo; R2 retains this. Config parse and native owner also need explicit same-route review.
findings.conclusion: Additional sudo semantics require actual same-valid-payload, non-root-policy oracle observations. This finding does not authorize removing arbitrary root checks.

limitations: Source review is not runtime parity.
The old archived openbao-plugin-auth-jwt repository was not used as the 2.7.1 oracle.
The existing 10 R1 and 5 R2 regression sources are not compilation or execution results.
Exact public web pages were unavailable to the search opener; official GitHub API source bytes were retrieved and pinned instead.
